subject: Quasar: sudden embeddings latency increase post-catalog update
messages:
From: Alice Zhou <alice.zhou@quasar.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: data-team@quasar.ai
Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 07:12:00 -0800
Subject: Embeddings latency spike after Jan 19 catalog change

Hi Priyom,

We started seeing a sharp increase in embeddings latency right after your model catalog update yesterday (Jan 19). Our p95 for single-vector embedding requests climbed from ~120ms to ~850-1,200ms and p99 spikes to 2-3s. This is across multiple regions (us-west primarily) and affects search freshness and real-time ranking.

Examples: attached latency graph and a small sample of x-request-ids (request-ids.txt). Impact: our real-time recommender times out for ~7% of lookups, and the backlog is causing throughput throttling on our side.

Can you investigate ASAP? We have a scheduled release at 11:00 PST and this could block it.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Zhou
Head of Data Platforms, Quasar Analytics
attachments: latency-graphs.png; request-ids.txt
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Zhou <alice.zhou@quasar.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 07:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Embeddings latency spike after Jan 19 catalog change

Hi Alice — thank you for the heads up and the artifacts. I'm escalating this to our engineering team now (cc'd). We opened incident INC-20270120-7 and will triage with highest priority.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- 30min triage call at 08:30 PST (please confirm)
- We'll try a rollback of the Jan 19 catalog mapping for your account behind a feature flag first (non-disruptive if we fail)
- Engineering will collect additional traces; please keep the sample request IDs you attached handy.

I apologize for the disruption — we'll provide hourly updates until resolved.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 08:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Embeddings latency spike after Jan 19 catalog change

Priyom / team — initial triage notes:

1) Correlation: catalog rollout at 2027-01-19T22:40:00Z included a change to variant routing rules: low-seq embeddings were being mapped to model-variant "m-embed-q4f" by default for several enterprise accounts (including Quasar) to reduce cost.
2) Observed behavior: that variant exhibits a long tail for short sequences on our current kernel combination (we see KV-cache cold paths, frequent fallback to slower matmul kernels). p95/P99 increases align with your timestamps/samples.
3) Customer traces: we pulled the x-request-ids from the attachment and see elevated server-side latencies on nodes running the q4f quantized variant.

Immediate ask for customer: can you confirm the typical sequence length distribution (avg tokens) for those calls? If they're usually <= 8 tokens, it explains the KV-miss pattern.

Mitigation options being considered (short list):
- Programmatic rollback of the variant mapping for Quasar (fast, high chance of improvement)
- Force fallback routing to the float16 variant for short sequences for 60m (higher cost)
- Temporary traffic steering to a different pool in us-west with warm caches

I'll start a rollback attempt on a small fraction and report metrics.

— Lauren
Sr. Engineer, Inference Runtime

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Exec summary & rollback approval request — Quasar latency impact

Marissa / Priyom — quick executive summary for leadership:

- Severity: customer-facing production degradation; p95 up ~6-7x, p99 spikes impacting SLOs and timeouts for Quasar's RT pipelines.
- Root cause hypothesis: catalog variant routing change to q4f quantized variant produced long-tail latencies for short sequences due to cold KV-cache and kernel path regressions.
- Impacted surface: embeddings hosted API for Quasar (us-west), possible cross-impact for other customers on same variant.

Recommended immediate action (seek approval to proceed):
1) Roll back the Jan 19 variant mapping specifically for account QSR-457 across us-west (target rollback complete in 30–60 minutes).
2) Offer Quasar one week of service credit and an engineer-on-call for their release at 11:00 PST.
3) Post-rollback: run a targeted A/B to validate p95/p99 restoration before closing inc.

If approved, I'll coordinate the rollback and patch the routing rules. Priyom — please clear the customer for the change and get go-ahead for credits.

— Markus
Director, Serving Platform
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Zhou <alice.zhou@quasar.ai>

Alice — update from the team: we have approval to run a targeted rollback of the catalog mapping for your account and to keep an engineer dedicated to your 11:00 PST release. Rollback will start in ~15 minutes and should be non-disruptive; we'll monitor closely.

Can you join us for a quick 20min check-in at 08:50 PST? Meeting: https://meet.redwood.ai/zoom/triage-20270120

We will also provide a formal incident brief after mitigation. Apologies for the disruption — we'll issue a one-week credit for affected calls.

Best,
Priyom
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Alice Zhou <alice.zhou@quasar.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 17:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Embeddings latency spike after Jan 19 catalog change — mitigation complete

All — final update: rollback completed at 16:12 PST. Post-rollback telemetry shows median ~115ms, p95 ~140ms, p99 ~320ms for Quasar's traffic in us-west — back within agreed SLOs and baseline variance.

Root cause (short): variant routing change mapped short-seq traffic to q4f quantized variant; the q4f kernel path had a cold-cache fallback for sequences <=8 tokens introduced by a kernel selector optimization in last week's runtime release. That combination created a new long tail for production short-seq workloads.

Action items (post-mortem prep):
- Revert kernel selector optimization for q4f short sequences; add regression test that runs short-seq synthetic workload against all quantized variants (owner: runtime team).
- Add per-account canary checks for catalog mappings and a synthetic embedding runner that exercises p95/p99 on each new mapping before rollout (owner: infra).
- Update SLAs/credits: Priyom to coordinate one-week credit and incident brief delivery.

I'll attach the incident brief and graphs to the final report.

— Lauren
